title: Personal repair list and question-level analysis from Paper 2
subject: English Language
source: Seeded from english-language/y11 lessons 55, 56, 57, 58, 60 (Personal repair list and question-level analysis from Paper 2 (pupil PDF))
intro: Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: in the portal response box, answer 'How does the writer use language and structure to present the danger?' , applying your fix
questions.a: Mark scheme points: calm claim overturned; 'thin silver line' (beauty and threat); shortening sentences; the sister's grip and 'four small bruises'; 'shoes full of sea'; ending erasing the road.
questions.model: Model opening: 'The writer presents the danger as sudden and silent: "It does not." contradicts the reassuring opening, and the tide arrives not as a wave but as "a thin silver line", lovely and lethal.'

questions.q: self-mark with the ladder and compare with your Paper 2 level
write one Q7-style sentence comparing 'The Causeway' with 'The Night the River Came In'
questions.a: For example: 'Both writers show water arriving with frightening speed, but the causeway memoir is about one family's escape, whereas the flood memoir is about a street pulling together.'

questions.q: Write your weakest reading question and the habit you will fix
questions.model: I do: in my analysis, Q6 lost most marks because I named techniques without effects, so my habit is 'which suggests...' after every quotation.

questions.q: Zoom into 'four small bruises' and explain the effect
questions.a: The precise, physical detail shows how frightened the sister was, and the danger's lasting mark.

questions.q: The best repair habit for Q3 and Q6 is...
questions.a: C) explaining the effect of every quotation
options: explaining the effect of every quotation

questions.q: Answer the ponder: which habit will add most marks?
questions.a: A named habit with a reason.

questions.q: in the portal response box, write the opening and two developed paragraphs of the speech
questions.a: Marked for AO1 (ideas from both texts transformed), AO4 (speech form, persuasive register for councillors), AO5 (accuracy and range).
questions.model: Paragraph model: 'Training costs little. A Saturday morning in the community hall, a list of who has a boat or a ladder, a phone tree: these are the things that turned strangers into a community in the past, and they can do it here.'

questions.q: self-mark against AO1, AO4 and AO5
Fill the planning grid with two more transformed ideas
questions.a: Two ideas from the texts in the speaker's own words.
questions.model: I do: I take the mill-hands' chain across the bridge and turn it into an action for councillors: 'keep a list of volunteers for every street'.

questions.q: Name one feature of form you will use
questions.a: For example: direct address to 'Councillors'; a call to action at the end.

questions.q: Section B rewards ideas that are...
questions.a: B) transformed into your own words
options: invented with no link to the texts

questions.q: Answer the ponder: copying, strength or weakness?
